---- Applicant  Versus State of Chhattisgarh Through P.S. Ramanujganj, District Balrampur- Ramanujganj (C.G.)
 --- Respondent _____________________________________________________________ For Applicant : Mr. Syed Ishhadil Ali, Advocate.

For State/ Respondent : Mr. Gary Mukhopadhyay,
G o v t .
 
A d v o c a t e ______________________________________________________________ Hon'ble Shri Justice Narendra Kumar Vyas Order on Board 17/01/2024 1.
Today the case is listed for hearing on admission since the case diary is available with the State counsel, as such the case is heard finally.

2. This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for grant of anticipatory bail, who has apprehension of being arrested in connection with Crime No. 200/2023, registered at Police Station- Ramanujganj, District Balrampur- Ramanujganj (CG) for the offence punishable under Sections 420,34 of the IPC.

3. Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that the complainant lodged complaint in Police Station Ramanujganuj alleging that he has given advance amount of Rs. 26,74,000/- to the company known as R.K. Paul, Ramesh Chand and Brother, 14 Pagayapati Street, Kolkata for delivery of umbrella.
It is alleged that despite persuasion made by him neither umbrella nor money was returned to him.

It is also alleged that when the complainant demanded his money, then the applicant and his father stated that they will supply the material till 20 th May, 2022 but they did not do so and have caused business loss to him thus the applicant committed the offence of cheating.

sentences.text: Counsel for the applicant would submit that the applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the case.
He would further submit that the applicant is only agent of the company not the director as such he cannot be held responsible for the said act.

To substantiate his submission,
he has submitted GST registration number of the company wherein the name of company has been mentioned as R.K. Paul and would pray for giving benefit of anticipatory bail.

5. On the other hand, counsel for the State opposes the bail application and would submit that from the statement recorded under Section 161 of the complainant wherein he has clearly made allegation against the applicant and would pray for rejection of the bail application.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
7.

Considering the fact of the case and material collected by the prosecution, further considering the statement recorded under Section 161 CrPC wherein the complainant has categorically stated that he has given money to Aakash Khanna and his father but no document has been filed to substantiate that he is not responsible for day today affairs of the company, prima-facie, involvement of the applicant is there, I am of the view that no case is made out for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.
8.
Accordingly, the present application under Section 438 of CrPC is rejected.

Sd/-
